pinned_source.title: Faster and More Dynamic Maximum Flow by Incremental Breadth-First Search
pinned_source.use: Algorithm description only; clean-room implementation, no upstream code or prose copied.

input.null_pointer_behavior: A null array pointer returns -1, including at declared input lengths 0 and 77.

output.definition: Maximum integral source-to-sink flow value, obtained as the capacity of the final EIBFS blocking cut.

workspace.meaning: Fixed 8-by-8 residual and original-capacity matrices; signed balances; two parent forests and distance labels; orphan queues; bounded parsing state.

algorithm_details.state: Capacity-respecting pseudoflow; positive excess roots are in the source forest, negative deficit roots in the sink forest, and all other vertices are free or non-root tree vertices.
algorithm_details.growth: Strictly alternate forward source-forest and reverse sink-forest phases; scan the current maximum-label frontier in ascending vertex/neighbor order and add free vertices one level deeper.
algorithm_details.connector_push: Use the four root/bottleneck cases in the paper: full connector residual for source/sink roots; otherwise cap by the relevant tree bottleneck and, when both roots are internal, by both root imbalance magnitudes.
algorithm_details.imbalance_repair: Drain sink-tree excesses toward their roots and source-tree deficits toward their roots; saturating a parent arc makes an orphan; round-robin adoption scans admissible parents then relabels to the minimum eligible residual-neighbor label or removes the vertex, transferring nonzero imbalance to the opposite forest.
algorithm_details.tie_policy: Ascending vertex IDs and matrix-neighbor IDs; first admissible parent; minimum qualifying parent label, then first neighbor at that label.
algorithm_details.result: Seed the blocking-cut side with every source-forest vertex, close it under residual reachability, and sum original capacities crossing to its complement. Each source-tree vertex is residual-reachable from its root; all positive-excess roots are in the source forest, all deficit roots (including the sink) are in the disjoint sink forest, and terminal growth separation makes this closure a minimum-cut certificate. This extraction applies §2 Lemma 1: any residual arc leaving the source forest has an active source-side tail during forward growth, while the symmetric reverse-growth invariant exhausts incoming residual arcs of the sink forest.
algorithm_details.complexity: EIBFS has O(N^2 M) worst-case time without dynamic trees; fixed bounds keep all state and scans bounded.

oracle_method: Primary: EIBFS two-forest pseudoflow growth, connector augmentation, excess/deficit draining, round-robin adoption, then the blocking cut rooted at all source-forest vertices and its residual closure. Independent: enumerate every source-containing, sink-excluding vertex subset and minimize directed cut capacity.
